extracted.intended_audience: registered patent practitioners, USPTO Office of Enrollment and Discipline staff, disciplinary counsel, and respondents in USPTO practitioner discipline matters
extracted.subtask_description: A USPTO Office of Enrollment and Discipline Final Order approving a settlement with a registered patent attorney that sets out stipulated facts, the legal conclusion (violation of 37 C.F.R. §10.77(c)), the agreed sanction (conditional suspension stayed, probation), supervisory and notification obligations, reporting deadlines, publication/redaction rules, and enforcement procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicability of professional conduct rules by date
rubrics_metrics.description: The USPTO Code of Professional Responsibility (37 C.F.R. §10.20 et seq.) applies to practitioner misconduct that occurred prior to May 3, 2013; the USPTO Rules of Professional Conduct (37 C.F.R. §11.101 et seq.) apply to practitioner misconduct occurring after May 2, 2013.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Determine which set of rules governs based on the date of the alleged misconduct; apply the older Code for pre-May 3, 2013 conduct and the newer Rules for post-May 2, 2013 conduct.

rubrics_metrics.name: USPTO jurisdiction for disciplinary proceedings
rubrics_metrics.description: The USPTO Director has jurisdiction over practitioner disciplinary matters pursuant to 35 U.S.C. §§2(b)(2)(D) and 32 and 37 C.F.R. §§11.19 and 11.26.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Disciplinary actions and settlement approvals arise under these statutory/regulatory authorities; pleadings and orders cite these provisions as jurisdictional bases.

rubrics_metrics.name: Duty not to neglect a legal matter (37 C.F.R. §10.77(c))
rubrics_metrics.description: A practitioner shall not neglect a legal matter entrusted to the practitioner (37 C.F.R. §10.77(c)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Failure to adequately supervise staff such that false submissions or other harmful conduct occur may constitute neglect of a legal matter and violate §10.77(c).

rubrics_metrics.name: Duty to adequately supervise non-lawyer assistants
rubrics_metrics.description: A practitioner who is responsible for supervision of a non-lawyer assistant must adequately supervise that assistant's activities in connection with prosecuting patent applications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a non-lawyer assistant submits false statements or forges signatures, the practitioner's inadequate supervision can be the basis for discipline even if the practitioner claims lack of actual knowledge.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on submission of false or fraudulent documents to the Office
rubrics_metrics.description: Submitting, with intent to deceive, knowingly false statements or doctored documents to the USPTO is misconduct.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples given include: fabricating e-mail confirmation messages to falsely show facsimile transmittal; affixing USPTO receipt stamps to postcards and submitting them as evidence of receipt; fabricating USPS Express Mail labels to misrepresent mailing dates; backdating certificates of mailing to show earlier mailing dates than actual.

rubrics_metrics.name: Responsibility for forged or unauthorized signatures and digital signatures
rubrics_metrics.description: A non-lawyer assistant signing a practitioner's signature (physically or by electronically “cut and pasted” digital versions) on papers filed with the Office implicates the practitioner's responsibility when the practitioner supervised that assistant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practitioners are accountable for signature integrity on filings; unauthorized or forged signatures attached by staff can support disciplinary findings for inadequate supervision or other violations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Registration requirement to practice before the USPTO
rubrics_metrics.description: A person not on the register of practitioners (37 C.F.R. §11.5) is not permitted to prosecute patent applications of others before the Office or represent others in proceedings before the Office unless reinstated to the register (37 C.F.R. §11.10(a)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a practitioner elects removal from the register, they lose authority to practice before the Office until successful reinstatement under 37 C.F.R. §11.7.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identification obligation for affected patent applications (three-condition test)
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent must use best efforts to identify each patent application prosecuted between January 1, 2004 and December 31, 2006 that meets all three conditions: (1) the Office received between those dates either (i) a petition to revive an abandoned application, (ii) a petition to withdraw the holding of abandonment, or (iii) a petition for extension of time where the petition's transmittal by the non-lawyer assistant preceded the Office receipt date by more than 30 days; (2) the non-lawyer assistant transmitted any paper in the application during that period; and (3) the Office issued a patent on the application at any time.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is a conjunctive identification requirement — all three conditions must be met to trigger the downstream client-notification and document-production obligations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Client notification and document production obligations
rubrics_metrics.description: For each present and former client identified for each affected application, the respondent must provide: (i) a copy of the April 10, 2014 declaration executed by the non-lawyer assistant with patent serial numbers redacted; and (ii) a copy of the redacted Final Order; and unambiguous written notification to clients of the specific false statements, potentially false statements, and potential backdating described in the referenced paragraphs of the April 10, 2014 declaration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Final Order lists many subparagraphs (i. through aa.) requiring specific unambiguous notifications tied to identified applications and particular paragraphs of the declaration (e.g., ¶14, ¶15, ¶16, ¶17). All client correspondence evidencing compliance must be preserved and produced to OED as set out below.

rubrics_metrics.name: Affidavit and submission to OED within 120 days
rubrics_metrics.description: Within 120 days after the Final Order is signed, respondent must submit to the OED Director: (1) an affidavit or declaration attesting to compliance with the terms of the Agreement and Final Order regarding client notifications (subparagraphs i. through aa.); and (2) copies of the client correspondence and written notifications evidencing compliance; correspondence submitted to OED shall be marked 'CONFIDENTIAL' and the OED shall keep it confidential.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Timely production of the affidavit/declaration plus the actual client correspondence is mandatory and will be used to assess compliance with notification obligations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conditional suspension and probation upon reinstatement
rubrics_metrics.description: If respondent seeks reinstatement under 37 C.F.R. §11.7, respondent shall be suspended from practice before the Office for 24 months in patent, trademark, and other non-patent matters, with the 24-month suspension stayed, and instead shall serve a 24-month period of probation commencing on the date reinstatement is granted. Respondent may practice during probation unless probation is revoked or other authority is lost.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The suspension is contingent and stayed; probation is the active supervisory sanction. Revocation of probation may result in entry of the stayed suspension.

rubrics_metrics.name: OED enforcement and Order to Show Cause procedure for alleged probation violations
rubrics_metrics.description: If the OED Director, in good faith, believes respondent failed to comply during probation with any provision of the Agreement, Final Order, or the USPTO Rules, the OED Director shall: (A) issue an Order to Show Cause why the USPTO Director should not immediately suspend respondent for up to 24 months for the violation; (B) send the Order to respondent at last address of record; and (C) grant respondent 30 days to respond. If, after consideration of the response, OED continues to believe respondent failed to comply, OED shall deliver the Order to Show Cause, respondent's response (if any), and supporting argument/evidence to the USPTO Director and request immediate suspension up to 24 months.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This sets the stepwise enforcement mechanism: show-cause, 30-day response window, referral to USPTO Director and requested suspension if noncompliance is sustained.

rubrics_metrics.name: OED may still seek discipline for the underlying misconduct
rubrics_metrics.description: Nothing in the Agreement/Final Order prevents the OED Director from seeking discipline for the misconduct leading to respondent's suspension.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Settlement does not preclude separate or additional disciplinary action for the same underlying facts if warranted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication and redaction of the Final Order
rubrics_metrics.description: The OED Director shall electronically publish the Final Order at the OED Reading Room and publish a notice in the Official Gazette materially consistent with the prescribed notice; however, the OED Director shall comply with 37 C.F.R. §11.59 except that patent application serial numbers shall be redacted from the Final Order.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Publication includes a summary notice for the Official Gazette that identifies the respondent, the sanction (conditional suspension/stayed, probation), a summary of misconduct, and mitigating considerations. Ensure serial numbers are redacted before public posting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Factors considered in mitigation and settlement
rubrics_metrics.description: In reaching the settlement, the OED Director took into consideration: (a) the non-lawyer assistant's misconduct occurred many years ago (2004–2006); (b) respondent cooperated with the investigation; and (c) respondent will take prompt action to notify present and former clients about the misconduct in patent applications where patents were granted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These are explicitly listed mitigating considerations that influenced the agreed sanction; similar factors may be cited in other disciplinary settlements to justify reduced or stayed penalties.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of disciplinary record in future proceedings
rubrics_metrics.description: Nothing in the Agreement/Final Order prevents the Office from considering the record of this disciplinary proceeding (1) when addressing any further complaint or evidence of the same or similar misconduct concerning respondent; and/or (2) in any future disciplinary proceeding against respondent as an aggravating factor and/or to rebut any statement or representation by or on respondent's behalf.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The record may be used offensively or defensively in later matters; practitioners should expect settled facts to be available for use in later discipline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Filing motion to dismiss pending disciplinary proceeding and cost allocation
rubrics_metrics.description: The OED Director shall file a motion with the administrative law judge requesting dismissal of the pending disciplinary proceeding within 14 days of the Final Order; the OED Director and respondent each shall bear their own costs incurred to date and in carrying out the terms of the Agreement and Final Order.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Settlement includes mutual cost allocation (each bears own costs) and prompt administrative steps to terminate the pending matter consistent with the Agreement.
